independentReview.root: Root independently viewed the whole unit, both words, all five complete target glyphs and controls and agreed to retain all five because the fused lower blobs do not separate competing classes. No source point is accepted.

inspections.finding: The bet retains its separately visible interior dagesh. Its broad bottom bar merges with a wide downward rectangular body; there is no surviving distinguishing lower stem or separated nodes that defeats compressed sheva, single-node, paired-dot and bar competitors. Clear bet sheva and hiriq and a plain final bet show the relevant alternatives. Retain the vowel note without asserting source absence.

The mem retains its separately visible interior dagesh. Its under-region is a broad horizontal slab connected to the letter base by a narrower bridge; one shallow lower projection does not uniquely distinguish a bar from a filled horizontal pair or compressed stem. The literal detached same-page mem patah, lamed tsere and qamats, and mem sheva are all compared at native pixels. The joined shape remains ambiguous; do not turn the bar-like appearance into an inferred vowel.

The vav has a continuous shaft and one rounded thickening at its lower endpoint. The same-page holam-vav control shows an ordinary rounded endpoint without an underpoint; the literal vav-sheva control has two additional vertically ordered swellings. A merged single point and ordinary terminal thickening remain competitors for this target. Retain without claiming either a point or its absence.

The pe has a broad body whose lower bar joins a large low rectangular lobe. No detached node, paired lateral contour, or independent stem survives strongly enough to exclude the other literal vowel classes. Compare the detached single-dot, horizontal-pair, bar, stem and three-node controls together with the complete source word. The expected word does not resolve the printing; retain.

The tsadi preserves its separate dagesh at the left of the diagonal. Its lower body and vowel region fuse into one wide block with only a shallow central lower notch. The literal same-unit tsadi segol has three identifiable joined nodes; the detached tsere has two identifiable side lobes, while bar and stem controls are distinct. The target notch alone cannot exclude a filled pair, bar or compressed three-node/stem impression. Retain the vowel note and the existing dagesh.
